jurisdiction.name: Libya
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Libya's AI governance is strategy-led and sits with the Tripoli-based Government of National Unity (GNU); the rival eastern-based government and the House of Representatives have issued no AI-specific instrument found online. The General Information Authority drafted a national AI strategy with ESCWA support in late 2025, and in 2026 the GNU created a Minister of State for Digital Economy and Artificial Intelligence, whose office issued the National AI Strategy 2026–2030, launched by Prime Minister Dbeibah on 1 June 2026 alongside a National Charter for AI Ethics. The strategy proposes a National AI Authority under the Council of Ministers, an AI ethics committee, explainable-AI guidance and a ban on AI for unlawful mass surveillance, but none of these has yet been created by an instrument published officially. There is no AI law and no general personal data protection law; the strategy itself names the legislative vacuum and targets a data protection law. Related binding texts exist only outside official portals (Cabinet Decision 40/2025 creating a National AI and Digital Transformation Programme; a 2025 Central Bank banking data-protection circular requiring impact assessments for AI) and are tracked as leads.
lead_institutions: Minister of State for Digital Economy and Artificial Intelligence (GNU)
General Authority for Communications and Informatics (GACI)
Council of Ministers, Government of National Unity
narrative.review_notes: Deep review 2026-10-07. Divided government: every recorded instrument was issued by GNU (Tripoli) bodies; parliament.ly (House of Representatives, Benghazi) shows only a committee (HoR Decision 115/2025) studying future laws on telecoms, data protection, cybersecurity and AI, with no draft text. Anti-Cybercrime Law 5/2022, Electronic Transactions Law 6/2022 and its NISSA-published implementing regulation, the GACI draft Communications and Informatics Law (2022 consultation), NISSA's cybersecurity strategy/controls, Cabinet Decision 358/2026 (National Authority for Cybersecurity and Digital Sovereignty), the GIA data governance documents, the National Government Digital Transformation Strategy 2023–2030 and the National Digital Development Agenda 2030 (Dec 2024; AI only as one emerging-tech line item, no AI pillar) were read or checked and contain no AI-specific provisions, so they are not recorded. lawsociety.ly is a non-official legal archive and was used only for discovery. cbl.gov.ly blocks search/API access (403) and loads circular lists dynamically; lawsociety.ly and dig.watch/unescwa.org returned 403 to automated fetching at times; pm.gov.ly appears compromised (spam links) and was not used. Earlier downloads in the previous attempt's scratch folder were not used as sources; all PDFs were re-fetched from gia.gov.ly.

instruments.official_title: الاستراتيجية الوطنية للذكاء الاصطناعي في دولة ليبيا (2026م – 2030م)
instruments.english_title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of the State of Libya 2026–2030
instruments.issuing_authority: Office of the Minister of State for Digital Economy and Artificial Intelligence, Council of Ministers (Government of National Unity)
instruments.current_status: Issued June 2026 by the Government of National Unity (Tripoli) under the supervision of the Minister of State for Digital Economy and AI; prepared by the General Information Authority with the General Authority for Communications and Informatics. Launched by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah on 1 June 2026 (GIA official page). Not issued by the eastern-based government or the House of Representatives. Strategy, not binding law.
instruments.summary: Libya's first adopted national AI strategy, organised in six pillars (governance and leadership, legislation and ethics, infrastructure and data, human capacity and education, innovation and priority sectors, monitoring and evaluation) with 6 strategic goals and 35 initiatives, prioritising health, education, financial services and public services. It proposes a National AI Authority (initially a national committee) under the Council of Ministers, a national AI ethics charter and ethics committee, explainable-AI guidance for public applications, a ban on AI for unlawful mass surveillance or discrimination, and a personal data protection law. Targets include AI use by 80% of government bodies and automating 50% of government transactions by 2030.
metadata_gaps: Exact day of issue in the document is month-level (June 2026); launch date 1 June 2026 taken from the GIA official news page

instruments.official_title: الاستراتيجية الوطنية للذكاء الاصطناعي في دولة ليبيا 2025-2030 (كانون الأول/ديسمبر 2025)
instruments.english_title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy in the State of Libya 2025–2030 (December 2025 version)
instruments.current_status: December 2025 text prepared by the General Information Authority (GNU, Tripoli) from consultations held in May 2025, with ESCWA methodology support; published on gia.gov.ly in February 2026. Superseded by the June 2026 final strategy (2026–2030). No adoption act for this version was found.
instruments.summary: Pre-adoption version of the national AI strategy, built on a May 2025 GIA consultation of national sectors and an ESCWA-designed survey. It sets out the six-pillar framework with 6 goals and 35 initiatives, proposes a National AI Authority starting from an interim national committee under the Council of Ministers chaired operationally by the GIA, and calls for a data protection and privacy law by 2026 and a national AI charter.
metadata_gaps: No formal adoption instrument located for this version

instruments.official_title: مقترح الاستراتيجية الوطنية للذكاء الاصطناعي في دولة ليبيا 2025-2030
instruments.english_title: Proposed National Artificial Intelligence Strategy in the State of Libya 2025–2030 (October 2025 draft)
instruments.current_status: Labelled 'proposal' (مقترح) and dated October 2025; published on gia.gov.ly. Replaced by the December 2025 version and then the June 2026 final strategy. No public consultation process is stated in the document.
instruments.summary: Draft proposal of Libya's national AI strategy prepared by the General Information Authority after May 2025 sector meetings. It introduces the six pillars, 6 goals and 35 initiatives and the four priority sectors (health, education, financial services, public services), and recommends a national AI body built on an interim national committee, national training programmes and a unified data-exchange platform.
metadata_gaps: Not a formal public consultation; drafting status only

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Searched gia.gov.ly, cim.gov.ly, nissa.gov.ly, cbl.gov.ly, gnu.gov.ly decisions database and parliament.ly in Arabic and English. No AI law, AI-specific risk/assurance, public-sector, procurement, cybersecurity, transparency, standards, sandbox, index, sectoral or generative-AI instrument with an official full text was found; no general data protection law exists. CBL Circular 18/2025 (AI impact assessment in banking) and Cabinet Decision 40/2025 lack official online text and are leads.
